title: Create and Commit to Your First Repo
description: Initialize a practice repository on your computer, create a text file, stage it, and commit it.
steps: Open your terminal and navigate to your practice folder (e.g., cd ~/Desktop or cd D:\)
Create a new directory and enter it: mkdir hcc-git-practice && cd hcc-git-practice
Initialize Git: git init (notice the hidden .git folder created)
Create a file hello.txt with the text 'Hello HCC!' inside
Run git status — notice hello.txt is listed in red under 'Untracked files'
Stage the file: git add hello.txt (or git add .)
Run git status again — notice it is now green under 'Changes to be committed'
Commit the change: git commit -m "Initial commit: Add hello.txt"
Run git status one last time — confirm it says 'nothing to commit, working tree clean'
expected_output: Terminal confirms '1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)' and git status reports a clean working tree.
tips: Never run git init inside your entire user home directory or Desktop root — always create a project subfolder first!
git add . stages all changes in the current directory, while git add filename stages only that specific file.
